items.title: SQLite foreign_keys pragma never enabled — declared cascade FKs not actually enforced
items.notes: Found 2026-07-20 by the BUG-33 schema brief. Original claim: src/backend/db/index.ts has no `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` anywhere, and plain SQLite disables FK enforcement by default per-connection — concluded that declared cascades were decorative only. CORRECTED 2026-07-20, same session: the BUG-32 backend brief independently hit this exact question (a real production 500 on deleting a place with items still referencing it — only possible if the FK constraint IS being enforced) and empirically verified via an isolated @libsql/client script that FK enforcement is ON by default with this driver, no explicit pragma needed. COO independently reproduced the same test directly (DELETE against a referenced parent row failed with SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_FOREIGNKEY) and confirms this. items.title: items.carriedFromItemId has no onDelete FK behavior — trip deletion 500s if a carried-forward item still references it
items.notes: Found 2026-07-21 by the WP-03/WP-04 Frontend brief (PR #208) while writing E2E coverage for the carried-forward tag — pre-existing defect, not introduced by that PR. Symptom: DELETE /api/trips/:id 500s if any of the trip's items was ever used as a carry-forward source (items.carried_from_item_id) for an item in ANY other trip, including trips since modified/locked/unlocked (the reference persists independent of trip status). Root cause: carriedFromItemId is a self-referencing FK (.references(() => items.id)) with no .onDelete(...) clause — SQLite/@libsql FK enforcement (confirmed ON by default, see BUG-38) defaults to RESTRICT. ARCHITECT RULING 2026-07-21 (ADL-36, jobs/architect/tech/20260307-architecture-decisions-log.md, GitHub issue #209, PR #212 merged): onDelete: 'set null' CONFIRMED (High confidence) — cascade rejected (would destroy an independent item on another trip), restrict is the bug. Verified safe against every current consumer: UpdateItemSchema does not expose the carry-forward fields (PATCH can't re-validate the coupling), the frontend tag reads the is_carried_forward boolean not the FK, no read path assumes carried_from_item_id non-null, and the partial index is already WHERE ... IS NOT NULL — NO backend/frontend change needed. The resulting is_carried_forward=1 / carried_from_item_id=NULL state is INTENTIONAL (create-time coupling per ADL-13 only; is_carried_forward is the permanent fact, the FK is a nullable provenance pointer). FK audit: BUG-39 is ISOLATED — every other no-onDelete FK references soft-deleted admin lists (never hard-deleted) or non-deletable geo/seed tables; items.tripPlaceId's omission is BUG-32's deliberate app-level reassign. No follow-up bug entry. IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-21 (PR #214, merged, all 9 CI checks green): carriedFromItemId FK now onDelete: 'set null' in schema.ts; migration 0011_majestic_nehzno.sql generated via db:generate/db:migrate (never db:push) — table-recreation SQL eyeballed, self-FK ON DELETE SET NULL / partial index idx_items_carried / all 3 chk_items_* CHECK constraints / existing row data all confirmed intact. schema.ts doc comment updated recording the intentional post-deletion state. Regression test added (trips.delete.test.ts) asserting DELETE /api/trips/:id returns 204 (was 500) with the derived item surviving, carried_from_item_id nulled, is_carried_forward unchanged — self-verified against a reverted fix to confirm it's a real regression guard. Deleting an individual source item directly was confirmed to hit the same constraint, also fixed by this change. GitHub issue #209 (closed via PR #214). Full discovery write-up: jobs/frontend/park-docs/20260721-FRONTEND-wp03wp04-park.txt.

items.title: Agent read-only diagnostic access to Railway, Turso, Clerk (ADL-33)
items.notes: Operational tooling, no BRD ID (ADL-33 §8). Triggered 2026-07-21 by manual log-relay pain during a live Railway deploy debug session. Architect ADL-33: Turso GRANT (clean, DB-scoped read-only tokens); Railway GRANT WITH CAVEAT (no read-only token scope exists); Clerk DO NOT GRANT. PO confirmed both. IMPLEMENTED (PR #181, merged): Turso + Railway hosts added to init-firewall.sh; .env.agent-diagnostics (gitignored) with both Turso tokens (verified via JWT claim inspection — distinct per-database `rid`, not account/group-scoped, after an initial false start with a mistakenly-pasted account-level token, flagged for revocation, never used) and both Railway tokens (one per environment — PO provided one for each rather than prod-only; verified via GraphQL auth — distinct environmentId per token confirms real per-environment scoping). scripts/agent-diagnostics/turso-query.mjs and railway-query.sh (read-only query runners) + runbook. Railway's official CLI does not work in this sandbox (no Linux aarch64 build) — railway-query.sh uses direct GraphQL calls (Project-Access-Token header) as the documented fallback. ALSO FOUND AND FIXED (ADL-34, same PR): init-firewall.sh fail-open bug — one dead static domain (statsig.anthropic.com, NXDOMAIN) aborted the whole script before the default-DROP lockdown was ever applied, leaving the container's outbound network fully unrestricted every container start. Fixed by moving lockdown before domain resolution. FIRST REAL USE (same session) surfaced the actual root cause of the original stuck-deploy problem: the Railway project's plan is `trial`, and Railway was actively deprioritizing Trial/Hobby deploys platform-wide during a demand spike (2026-07-21, confirmed via Railway status/community reports) — not a code/config issue. Flagged to Ryan: confirm the Hobby-plan upgrade from ADL-32 actually completed; Pro tier is the only tier that fully bypasses the deploy queue. FOLLOW-UP (2026-07-21, ADL-34 §5): the container rebuild happened and surfaced a second bug in the same fix — GitHub itself failed the final verification (`unable to reach https://api.github.com`). Root cause: lockdown-before-resolution now blocks step 6's own `curl https://api.github.com/meta` bootstrap fetch (chicken-and-egg — GitHub's IPs aren't allowlisted yet because that fetch is what's supposed to allowlist them). Fixed by DNS-bootstrapping api.github.com's IP via `dig` (same pattern as the Turso/Railway entries) before the curl call. VERIFIED 2026-07-22: Ryan rebuilt the container since this fix; the following COO session made dozens of successful `gh` CLI calls throughout (gh pr create/merge, gh issue create/close, gh run list/view, across ~10 PRs) with zero firewall/DNS errors — direct end-to-end confirmation the GitHub-bootstrap fix holds post-rebuild. items.title: test-db.ts hand-mirrors 21 CREATE TABLE statements — silent schema-drift risk in every repository test
items.notes: Logged 2026-07-26 (COO) during the OP-15 prerequisite audit. Was previously untracked — it existed only as a sub-bullet inside OP-15's notes ('Q22 test-DDL consolidation'), so deferring OP-15 would have buried it. src/backend/repositories/__tests__/test-db.ts imports db/schema.ts for Drizzle typing but then hand-writes all 21 tables as literal DDL. A migration can therefore change the real schema while every repository test keeps passing green against the stale copy — the tests would not detect the drift. Same family as the stale local dev.db that caused a false alarm during the 2026-07-26 BUG-63 investigation (companions missing user_id post-migration 0012). Count has grown from the 13 recorded in OP-15's notes to 21, so this is actively worsening. Fix direction: drop the hand-written DDL and apply the real migrations to the in-memory libSQL DB (migrate(db, { migrationsFolder: 'src/backend/migrations' })) so the test schema is identical to production's by construction. IMPLEMENTATION CAVEAT for the brief: createTestDb() runs in beforeEach across ~580 backend tests, so replaying 12+ migration files per test may hurt suite time — build the schema once and clone per test rather than re-migrating. Also clears OP-15 prerequisite (a); sequence this BEFORE the OP-15 skills design pass. Scheduled as batch B9 in jobs/COO/backlog-clearance-plan.md. DONE 2026-07-28 — B9, issue #291, PR #292. test-db.ts now applies the real migrations to a throwaway template :memory: DB, lifts the resulting DDL from sqlite_master (excluding __drizzle_migrations and sqlite_% internals), caches it at module scope, and replays it per test via client.batch() — so the schema is migration-derived by construction while paying the migration cost once, not per test. Suite runtime 6.75s -> 6.91s, noise-level. Drift detection DEMONSTRATED, not just asserted: adding a DROP COLUMN to migration 0012 made all 17 companions tests fail; before this change that same edit had zero effect on any repository test. Verified independently by COO against the diff. FOUND EN ROUTE: items.test.ts used status 'booked' in 8 places — never valid against chk_items_status and absent from all application code; the old CHECK-free hand-written DDL had masked it for the life of the file. Corrected to 'confirmed'. SCOPE LIMIT — see QUAL-17: this fixed test-db.ts only, and 15 further test files hand-roll the same DDL independently, so route-level tests are NOT yet drift-safe.

Original note (2026-03-23 backfill, wrong) is superseded by this one; its exact text is recoverable from git history on this file rather than repeated here, per the negative-findings rule (CLAUDE.md).

SPEC'D 2026-07-28 — ADL-46, GitHub issue #326 (Architect), branch chore/adl46-access-model. The creation-scope gap this note identified as 'a separate brief per ADL-28 Question 5' is that brief, and BUG-63 turned out to be the same defect filed twice. THE ANSWER IS NOT 'OPEN CREATION TO NON-OWNERS': on PO direction, categories and activities become PER-USER — a userId NOT NULL FK, UNIQUE(user_id, name) replacing the current global UNIQUE(name), existing rows backfilled to the owner, and a lazy seed from the global defaults on first access so a new user is never blank. Any user can add custom entries') contradicted SE-03 on the same routes and is replaced wholesale — proposed v3.13 text in ADL-46 section 6.3, for the COO to apply. Pre-conditions: (a) RESOLVED 2026-07-28 — the PO confirmed that a user deactivates entries in their OWN list and the owner's retained authority covers global reference data only; the deciding argument was AD-03, which is unsatisfiable for a non-owner otherwise, so the proposed AD-09 text stands unchanged; (b) the migration must preserve `id` through the CROSS JOIN because trip_categories_map FKs to it, and staging must be queried for category/activity mappings on non-owner trips first — the Architect expects zero since the picker has always 403'd, but flagged that as an inference with a named blind spot (POST /api/trips accepts category_ids under requireAuth alone), not a verified fact.

UPDATED 2026-07-29 AFTER THE OP-27 REVIEW. (b) is now partly settled and partly widened. A count is also point-in-time and the migration runs later, so ADL-46 section 9.3.3 additionally requires a RAISE(ABORT) assertion inside the migration file that fails if any junction row crosses a user boundary — turning a pre-check into a run-time invariant. items.title: Any authenticated user can add a city via constrained find-or-create (GE-16)
items.notes:
Created 2026-07-30 by the BRD v3.13 bump (ADL-46 BRD gate) — new requirement ID, so per the BRD->tracker rule it gets its own tracker entry with success criteria. GE-16 is the BRD home for the ADL-46 cities decision: any authenticated user adds a not-yet-catalogued city through a constrained find-or-create path (never a free-for-all POST), with server-side geocode resolution building the row from the service's canonical response, coordinates never client-supplied. Three end states — resolved (matched; global-visible with coordinates), pending (unanswered: offline/error/not-yet-attempted; creator-private, retried to a cap), unresolvable (geocoder said no match; creator-private, NEVER retried). Correction is at the PLACE level (re-point city_id), never a write to a shared global row. City identity = (name COLLATE NOCASE, country_code, COALESCE(region_id,0)) so Springfield IL + MO coexist while the COALESCE sentinel guards BUG-33; multi-result asks the user (populates the region selector AddPlaceFlow already renders) rather than guessing. Full measurable success criteria are in the BRD (GE-16 row, v3.13) — not duplicated here to keep one canonical home. IMPLEMENTATION: this is ADL-46's cities work, spanning the S2/S4 stages — Database (cities table recreation absorbing the geocode_status/geocode_attempts amendments + the identity index change), then Backend (find-or-create with the wildcard-upgrade middle step, resolve-then-create, retry classification, geocoding proxy for BUG-55), then Frontend. Ships as ONE RELEASE with BUG-63/BUG-55/AD-09 per PO sequencing. BLOCKS the BUG-63 P1 unblock on its cities half. Implementer trap (from the park doc): the find-or-create middle step — wildcard-upgrade a region-less row rather than duplicate it — is what re-creates BUG-33 if omitted. Not yet dispatched: the Database brief is the first of the three ADL-46 briefs.

DATABASE BRIEF IN PROGRESS 2026-07-30 — GitHub issue #332, branch feat/adl46-s3s4-migrations. Status -> in_progress. Delivers ADL-46 S3+S4 SCHEMA + MIGRATIONS ONLY (schema.ts changes, two hand-written migrations, pre-migration checks); Backend/Frontend are separate briefs. schema.ts: trip_categories + activities are now per-user (user_id NOT NULL FK ON DELETE CASCADE, UNIQUE(user_id,name)); cities gains geocode_attempts (DEFAULT 0), created_by_user_id (nullable FK ON DELETE SET NULL — deliberate), the amended geocode_status CHECK adding 'unresolvable', and the D13 identity index uniq_cities_name_country_region_ci = (name COLLATE NOCASE, country_code, COALESCE(region_id,0)) replacing uniq_cities_name_country_ci. Migrations: 0014 (S3, trip_categories + activities recreation, id-preserving CROSS JOIN-to-owner backfill) and 0015 (S4, cities recreation). Both hand-written — the generated SQL was discarded (0014's ADD NOT NULL REFERENCES is unappliable per review F2; 0015's generated INSERT...SELECT pulled columns absent from the old table and MANGLED the COALESCE expression index, an ADL-15 drizzle-kit bug). Verified locally on a scratch DB from the real migration chain: id preserved, all three junction map rows survive, PRAGMA foreign_key_check clean, amended CHECK accepts 'unresolvable', D13 index allows same-name/diff-region and rejects same-region + case-fold + both-NULL-region duplicates. SELF-VERIFYING ASSERTION MECHANISM DEVIATION: ADL-46 §9.3.3's literal SELECT RAISE(ABORT,...) WHERE EXISTS(...) is INVALID SQLite ('RAISE() may only be used within a trigger-program' — the review appendix never executed the assertions, so it wasn't caught); preserved the intent with a CASE-into-named-CHECK scratch table that genuinely aborts+rolls back, verified firing on a seeded cross-user place-activity row (all THREE junction tables guarded, incl. trip_place_activities_map via trip_places). PRE-MIGRATION CHECK (§9.3.2) RUN AGAINST BOTH STAGING AND PRODUCTION via turso-query.mjs — all clean: trip-level non-owner mappings 0/0, place-level non-owner mappings 0, is_owner=1 count EXACTLY 1 (CROSS JOIN backfill deterministic) on both. KNOWN CROSS-BRIEF BREAKAGE (expected, flagged not fixed per brief scope): the per-user schema change breaks type:check:backend (20 errors) and test:backend (34 tests) at every category/activity insert site missing user_id (admin.ts, startup.service.ts, seed.ts, reset-staging.ts + trips/lock-matrix/qa-backend-fixes tests) — all NOT NULL user_id, all Backend-brief scope (lazy seed + insert handlers), none cities-related. CI will be red on those until the Backend brief lands; the DB deliverable itself is verified green. RELEASE ASSEMBLED 2026-08-01 on release/adl46-access-model, four stages all green: DB (#333), QA ATDD red acceptance tests (#336), Backend (#338), Frontend (#341). Then an OP-27 fresh-eyes review of the *assembled* release (#342) returned SHIP WITH FOLLOW-ONS with one HIGH finding (F1 — ambiguous lookups auto-resolved to candidates[0] and were promoted to the shared catalogue, violating two GE-16 success criteria); Architect ruling R1-R4 (#343) and its Backend implementation (#345/#346) fixed it plus a shipped regression the ruling surfaced (resolveCityName marked a lookup ambiguous whenever 2+ candidates shared the requested region, so the happy path produced pending rows with no map pin). Status -> done_pending_uat on merge to main. UAT MUST COVER: pending cities shade their country but show NO pin and NO region shading (all three states verified, ruling S5) — this is specified behaviour, not a defect; and the live Nominatim egress path is UNVERIFIED from the devcontainer (firewall), so real geocode lookups need exercising on staging (ENV-01). Follow-ons NOT in this release, tracked separately: QUAL-23 (review F3 — zero-owner migration commits dangling FKs; mitigated, live pre-checks pass on staging and prod today), QUAL-21 (F4 — resolve-then-create success path has zero route-level coverage; the root cause of both defects this release's review caught), QUAL-22 (F8 — QA suite geocoding mock drifted; one group passes only because a try/catch swallows a TypeError), BUG-69 (frontend retry queue never terminates on 'unresolvable'), BUG-70 (Companion.is_active type lie). PARTIAL DELIVERY — READ BEFORE GIVING A UAT VERDICT: one GE-16 success criterion is NOT satisfied by this release. GE-16 requires that a user who mistypes a city name can correct the affected place without losing its items or activity tags and without owner intervention. The backend half shipped (PATCH place accepts city_id, ADL-46 D11, preserves items and tags) but there is NO FRONTEND for it — verified two ways, and independently reached by the UX agent. So a user still cannot correct a wrong city. Tracked as UX-12 with the UX spec's deliberately-small MVP. Treat GE-16 the way TR-14 was treated when BUG-50 shipped without the review_pending delete path: passing UAT on the rest does not close the requirement.

items.notes:
BRD v3.0 §6, success criteria added v3.2. Hosting before multi-user; supersedes local-only NF-01 and OneDrive NF-04. Railway (compute) + Turso (database) per ADL-32, resolves OQ-04. Deployment shakedown 2026-07-20/21 surfaced five sequential blockers, each masking the next until fixed — full root-cause detail lives in each PR's description, not restated here:
1. Railway trial-plan deploy queue (external — Railway was platform-wide deprioritizing Trial/Hobby deploys during a demand spike; cleared on its own). Detail: jobs/architect/tech/20260721-agent-diagnostics-runbook.md.
2. Missing `db:migrate` before server start — ADL-32 §5 specified it, PR #175/#176 never wired it in, so the Turso prod DB was connected to but never schema-migrated. Fixed PR #185.
3. Frontend/Clerk env vars were never set on Railway at all initially; once added, Helmet's CSP (`scriptSrc: ["'self'"]`) blocked Clerk's browser SDK entirely (never exercised before since the frontend previously only ran via Vite's dev server, not this Express app). Fixed PR #187 (added CLERK_ORIGIN to scriptSrc/connectSrc).
4. Once sign-in worked, CSP still blocked Clerk's background-token Web Worker (blob: URL, no worker-src set) and the user's avatar (img.clerk.com, not in imgSrc). Fixed PR #189.
5. Map/trips tabs still errored (`Unexpected token '<'... not valid JSON` — a fetch expecting JSON got the SPA's index.html instead). Root cause: `VITE_API_BASE_URL` resolved to a non-empty garbage value (Railway variable set to a literal placeholder string instead of truly empty/absent), so every request became `fetch("<value>/api/trips")` — a path that never matches `/api/*` and falls through to the SPA catch-all. This meant zero authenticated requests had EVER reached the backend, which also explains why the admin tab never appeared (not a separate OWNER_CLERK_ID bug). Fixed PR #190 — apiClient.ts now coerces an unset var to `''` via `??`, so it's safe regardless of exactly what Railway stores.

CONFIRMED WORKING 2026-07-21 (Ryan, live on prod): sign-in, map tab, admin panel, and trips tab all render correctly. Prod `users` table confirmed via turso-query.mjs: 1 row, is_owner=1. Trips list is empty — expected, fresh prod DB with no trips entered yet, not a bug. This closes the 'Clerk sign-in e2e', 'CI+deploy green on merge to main', and 'data persists across a deploy' strands of ADL-32 §10.

CONFIRMED WORKING 2026-07-21 (Ryan, cellular): prod URL reachable and functional over HTTPS from phone/cellular network — closes remaining item (3). Ryan also created a second user account with no issues — multi-user signup path confirmed working end-to-end (extends the data-separation confirmation from the 2026-07-16 UAT session to a live prod sign-up, not just an existing test account).

items.title: UK constituent countries (Scotland etc.) unavailable when adding a place
items.notes: Found 2026-07-20 UAT. Countries are ISO 3166-1 (countryCode is the PK, e.g. 'US','AU') — Scotland/England/Wales/Northern Ireland aren't countries under that standard, they'd be Regions under GB, same tier as US states/AU provinces (GE-01/02/06). GB appears missing from seed data entirely, or seeded without region_tier_enabled — either way this is a gap against GE-04/05 ('every country ships pre-configured, defaults applied automatically on first launch'). Fix: seed GB/'United Kingdom' with region_tier_enabled=1, region_tier_label likely 'Constituent Country', and add Scotland/England/Wales/Northern Ireland as regions. P1 — the Scotland dogfood trial (BRD-PL0104 trigger) needs this working. GitHub issue #154. DISPATCHED 2026-07-20 to database agent, branch fix/bug30-uk-region-seed. PR opened 2026-07-20: #168, Closes #154, all 9 CI checks green. Root cause: GB was present with region_tier_enabled=0. Fix: region_tier_enabled=1 + label 'Constituent Country', added England/Scotland/Wales/NI as regions (GB-ENG/SCT/WLS/NIR) via data-only custom migration, guarded to only patch already-seeded installs (self-caught a fresh-install idempotency bug in first draft — startup.service.ts seedRegions() would have been starved on a truly fresh install). Flagged: possible 5th drizzle-kit@0.31.9 bug (migrate CLI transiently dropped the new migration's journal entry once, not reproduced after) — noted in memory for future watching, not yet confirmed as a real/reproducible bug. MERGED to main 2026-07-20 (PR #168, squash), main CI confirmed green post-merge.

items.title: Duplicate city entries in place autocomplete (Glasgow appeared twice)
items.notes: Found 2026-07-20 UAT. `cities` table has no uniqueness constraint on (name, country_code) — the geocoding/lookup path is creating a new row instead of finding the existing one. Fix: find-or-create by (name, country_code) case-insensitive, plus a unique index to prevent recurrence; needs a data cleanup pass for existing duplicates. GitHub issue #157. DISPATCHED 2026-07-20: database (branch fix/bug33-city-dedup-schema) + backend (branch fix/bug33-city-dedup-logic), parallel. Backend PR opened 2026-07-20: #167, Closes #157. POST /api/cities now finds-or-creates by (name, country_code) case-insensitive before inserting. 3 new tests + full suite green, CI mostly green (E2E pending as of this note). Independent of the parallel DB-brief unique index. Schema half PR opened 2026-07-20: #169, Closes #157, BRD GE-11, all 9 CI checks green. Adds UNIQUE(name COLLATE NOCASE, country_code) on cities (uniq_cities_name_country_ci) plus a data-cleanup migration merging existing duplicates (canonical = lowest id, geocode fields coalesced from best-resolved dup, trip_places/items/trip_place_activities_map re-pointed, collision with uniq_trip_places_trip_city handled by keeping the earlier trip_place row). Architect consulted before implementation per the schema-change-review rule (COLLATE NOCASE mechanism + trip_places collision-handling ruling). Verified against a throwaway copy of real dev.db duplicate data before writing the real migration. IMPORTANT for the parallel backend brief (fix/bug33-city-dedup-logic): its find-or-create lookup must match COLLATE NOCASE or it'll miss the canonical post-merge row and throw on insert. Schema half MERGED to main 2026-07-20 (PR #169, squash, renumbered to migrations 0009/0010 to resolve the BUG-30 idx collision), main CI confirmed green. Logic half (PR #167) hit a merge conflict, owning agent resolving as of this note. Logic half MERGED to main 2026-07-20 (PR #167, squash), main CI confirmed green post-merge. items.title: Time-varying CI checks must not gate deploys — Dependency Vulnerability Scan excluded from the production branch
items.notes: ADL-40 (2026-07-26). Trigger: production deploys blocked outright — `Security Checks` failed on production@299ab5c (run 30210259329) on GHSA-v422-hmwv-36x6 (body-parser, HIGH), and Railway gates prod deploys on CI green. Root cause is NOT the promotion: `npm audit` queries the advisory DB at run time, so the identical tree passed on main 2026-07-24 and failed on production 2026-07-26 (verified — `git diff 299ab5c 3889436 -- package-lock.json package.json` is empty; only drift-ledger/STATUS.md/tracker.json/park-doc changed between them). Deployability had become a function of the calendar. Fix: security.yml push trigger `branches: ["**"]` → `branches-ignore: ["production"]`; ci.yml deliberately unchanged and still gates prod. Does not weaken security — check runs attach to a commit SHA not a branch, and production is only ever fast-forwarded from main, so every promoted SHA already carries this workflow's green statuses; the re-run is skipped, the verdict is frozen at the point it was earned. Detection unchanged on PRs and main (how DEP-01/DEP-02 were both found). Residual accepted gap: a direct push to production bypassing main would be unscanned — contained by process (CLAUDE.md: production is ff-only, agents never touch it). Alternative of removing Railway's CI gate entirely rejected by PO. Deferred idea, not adopted: a scheduled nightly audit on main that opens an issue, which would also catch advisories landing against an unchanged main between PRs. Production promoted to ce5dbd5 same session, CI + Security Checks both green, deploy gate reopened. security-backlog.md bumped to v1.3 with a pointer section, same PR.

items.title: No wholesale rewrites of shared-record files — append/amend only, hook-enforced (warn)
items.notes: PO direction 2026-07-28: 'agents should never fully rewrite anything, if a full rewrite is required there is a fundamental issue/deviation and I'd want it double checked' — with an explicit invitation to calibrate, since a blanket rule may be too strict. Trigger: Wave 1 sub-wave A ran B1 and B2 as concurrent Frontend agents and BOTH rewrote jobs/frontend/context/current.txt in full. Each rewrite was individually reasonable and each silently dropped the other's thread record; it surfaced only as the PR #303 merge conflict, hand-resolved by the COO keeping both entries. RECURRENCE, not a one-off: the Wave 0 concurrency notes record the same file colliding in 3 of 4 concurrent agents for the same reason, and the fix identified then (per-agent region / append-don't-rewrite) was never adopted. Twice across two waves cleared the D-03 bar. Calibration adopted, scoped by file class rather than blanket: (a) SHARED-RECORD files are append/amend-only, never wholesale replacement — jobs/**, _project/tracker.json, the BRD, the ADL log, the backlog clearance plan, .planning/**, CLAUDE.md; mechanically 'use Edit not Write on an existing one'. (b) SOURCE CODE full-file rewrites stay allowed but must be DECLARED in the completion report with a reason, so the COO can double-check — a small module legitimately changing in full is normal work and blocking it would be noise. Implemented: .claude/hooks/no-wholesale-rewrite.sh (PostToolUse, Write matcher, fires only when git already tracks the path so new-file creation is silent), wired in .claude/settings.json, canary added to /coo-startup step 0 (both the warn case and the Edit-stays-silent case). Tested 6 cases, all passed. Root-cause fix beyond the hook: all 8 jobs/<role>/<role>-system-prompt.txt files said 'Update jobs/<role>/context/current.txt with current state' as an end-of-thread step — that instruction was itself producing the rewrites, and now reads 'APPEND a new dated entry ... never rewrite the file wholesale'. Warn-not-block per OP-26's precedent; revisit once the false-positive rate is known.

items.title: Negative-findings rule binds every role including the COO — hook extended to cover COO-authored briefs
items.notes: PO direction 2026-07-28: 'you as the COO also need the negative findings piece, it should apply to the whole team.' Trigger: the rule failed again on the very next wave after being adopted. Brief B2 (issue #298) asserted that AD-09's owner-only deactivation 'is not enforced on the backend today' and bundled a go-enforce-it backend task on that premise. FALSE — adminRouter.use(requireOwner) at src/backend/routes/admin.ts:105 registers BEFORE the categories/activities sub-routers mount at :232-233, so every PATCH/DELETE was already owner-gated, and security.access-matrix.test.ts already had passing non-owner-403 tests for exactly it. The claim came from the backlog clearance plan §7 and the COO propagated it into the brief without re-probing. Caught only because the brief itself instructed the agent to double-probe; the agent ran three probes and corrected the tracker note instead of writing code. Same shape as the router.delete failure already recorded in CLAUDE.md — both COO failures, not agent ones. TWO FIXES. (1) Written rule: CLAUDE.md now states no role is exempt, the COO explicitly included, and that a claim inherited from an existing project document is NOT pre-verified — age is not evidence. Added to all 8 role system prompts. (2) Enforcement gap closed: the OP-26 hook matched only Write|Edit, but the COO does not write briefs to files — it writes them into GitHub issue bodies via Bash, so the single highest-leverage place for a false absence was the one place the hook could not see. negative-findings-guard.sh now also scans `gh issue create` / `gh pr create` / `gh issue comment` bodies (Bash matcher added in settings.json). PATTERN SET WIDENED, found by testing rather than assumed: the original regex missed BOTH phrasings that actually caused this project's false premises — 'is not enforced' and 'there is no X' — so absence-of-enforcement language ('not enforced', 'not gated', 'not validated', 'no call sites', 'there is no', 'there are no', 'never wired') is now covered. 6 test cases pass, including both historical false premises. Canary added to /coo-startup step 0 for the brief path specifically.

items.title: Scanner suppressions need COO sign-off — reword your own text first
items.notes: PO direction 2026-07-28, agreeing with the COO recommendation ('agree on rewording and flagging the instance'). Trigger: during B2 (PR #303), Gitleaks' generic-api-key rule flagged the literal string 'Categories/Activities/Countries' in a tracker note the agent had just authored — a genuine false positive, three capitalised words joined by slashes matching an entropy/shape heuristic. The agent resolved it by adding .gitleaks.toml and went green. THE CONFIG IS KEPT and is sound on inspection: [extend] useDefault = true keeps every standard rule active, and the allowlist is an exact-string regexTarget='match' on that one 50-character phrase — not a path exemption, not a file exemption, not a commit exemption. The PRECEDENT is what needed a decision: an implementation agent independently weakening a SECURITY SCANNER's configuration to turn a red check green is not a call an implementation brief carries, however narrow the change, and the cheaper fix was available — reword its own changelog note. Rule adopted: (a) when a scanner flags content you just authored and it is a false positive, fix your own text first; (b) never add or widen a scanner suppression — .gitleaks.toml allowlists, new nosemgrep comments, npm audit exceptions, lint disables — without COO sign-off, stop and report instead; (c) pre-existing nosemgrep annotations carrying a stated reason (e.g. the requireAuth-applied-globally comments in src/backend/routes/) are unaffected, this governs NEW suppressions; (d) any suppression the COO does approve carries a comment naming what was flagged, why it is a false positive, and how that was verified — as .gitleaks.toml now does. Recorded in CLAUDE.md and all 8 role system prompts.

items.title: City markers render behind state shading layer
items.notes: Found 2026-07-21 UAT, logged only — not yet briefed. When state shading activates it visually covers city tag markers — layer/z-order issue, city markers should stay on top. FIXED 2026-07-28 (GitHub #296, PR #301, Wave 1 sub-wave A brief B1). Root cause was not CSS or JSX order: RegionLayer, CountryLayer and CityMarkers are all native MapLibre GL layers, so paint order is the order layers were ADDED to the style. CountryLayer and CityMarkers mount unconditionally on MapView's first render; RegionLayer mounts lazily once zoom crosses REGION_ZOOM_THRESHOLD and region data loads, and MapLibre's addLayer with no beforeId always inserts at the top of the stack — so region shading landed above city-markers the moment it activated, despite CityMarkers appearing later in MapView's JSX. Fix: beforeId: 'city-markers' on regionFillLayer, which the Layer component honours on both initial addLayer and later moveLayer, so it holds across remounts as the user zooms. COO verified the failure mode this fix could have had — a beforeId naming a layer that does not exist throws — and it cannot occur: MapView.tsx:160 mounts CityMarkers unconditionally and CityMarkers always renders its Source+Layer (empty FeatureCollection when there are no trips). Region outline is a fill-outline-color paint property, not a second layer, so one beforeId covers it. Regression test at src/frontend/components/Map/__tests__/RegionLayer.test.ts. Stale doc comment at MapView.tsx:6 ('zoom >= 4' vs the constant's 3) fixed in the same PR per the document lifecycle rule. brdRefs backfilled to MP-02, the governing requirement ('zooming in on the map reveals region-level shading and city-level pins') — flagged by the B1 agent, verified against the BRD by the COO before adding. REGION_ZOOM_THRESHOLD and the 39 MB region payload deliberately untouched (BUG-48 / ADL-44).

items.title: City entry doesn't auto-populate country/state — CSP blocks the Nominatim call (deployment defect)
items.notes:
Found 2026-07-21 UAT, logged only — not yet briefed. Entering a city name doesn't auto-fill its country/state fields — likely the geocode/lookup path isn't wired to populate those fields on selection. RECLASSIFIED AS A REGRESSION 2026-07-28 (PO): 'country and state/region as that's how it was working previously'. This is NOT an unbuilt feature — the brief leads with diagnosing what broke it (git history over the geocode/city-selection path), not building it from scratch. BRD gate cleared at v3.12: GE-15 already covered the country half and was extended to cover region/state where GE-03 has the Region tier enabled. VERIFICATION CONSTRAINT (ENV-01): Nominatim is firewall-blocked in this devcontainer, so the live geocode path CANNOT be exercised here — any agent claim that the path 'works' or 'is broken' based on a live call is unreliable by construction. ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-07-28 (COO, two independent probes) — THIS IS A DEPLOYMENT/CONFIG DEFECT, NOT A PRODUCT BUG, AND NOT A FRONTEND BRIEF. The feature is fully built and looks correct: AddPlaceFlow.tsx:183-208 auto-populates country AND region (GE-15/UX-04) from lookupCityCountry(). Probe 1: src/frontend/hooks/useCities.ts:14,46 shows the BROWSER fetches https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/search directly — it is not proxied through the backend. Probe 2: helmet's CSP connectSrc at src/backend/server.ts:128-130 is [self, *.maptiler.com, CLERK_ORIGIN] — nominatim.openstreetmap.org is absent. So in any environment where the backend serves the app with helmet applied, that fetch is CSP-blocked; AddPlaceFlow.tsx:206's bare .catch() swallows the failure with no user feedback and no logging, and the fields silently stay blank. It works under the Vite dev server (different origin, no helmet CSP), which is exactly why the PO reports it 'was working previously' and why no test caught it — every test runs in the dev/jsdom path. SECOND DEFECT IN THE SAME FUNCTION: useCities.ts:47 sets a 'User-Agent' header, which is a forbidden header name for browser fetch() and is silently dropped by the browser — Nominatim's usage policy requires an identifying UA, so even with CSP fixed, direct browser calls are exposed to throttling/blocking. Both defects point the same way: the lookup likely belongs behind a backend proxy route rather than a CSP allowlist entry. That is a SEC-01/external-integration call — needs an Architect pass before implementation, per the infra/runtime guardrail. PULLED OUT OF BRIEF B4 2026-07-28 for this reason.

CONFIRMED LIVE 2026-07-28 — diagnosis upgraded from inference to observed fact. Ryan captured the staging browser console while adding a place; it contains the violation verbatim: "Connecting to 'https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/search?q=denver&format=json&limit=1&addressdetails=1' violates the following Content Security Policy directive: connect-src 'self' *.maptiler.com https://just-raptor-89.clerk.accounts.dev. The action has been blocked." That is a third, fully independent probe (browser runtime, staging) agreeing with the two code-read probes above, and it quotes the deployed connect-src allowlist matching src/backend/server.ts:128-130 exactly. The ENV-01 verification constraint noted above is therefore no longer blocking: the defect is established without needing to reach Nominatim from this devcontainer. Also confirms the silent-failure half — the console shows the block but the UI gave no feedback, exactly as AddPlaceFlow.tsx:206's bare .catch() predicts. RECOMMENDED SCOPE: bundle the Architect pass with BUG-63, which the same console session surfaced — both are the same question (which external and global-reference surfaces are reachable by whom).

ARCHITECT PASS DONE 2026-07-28 — ADL-46, GitHub issue #326, branch chore/adl46-access-model. Spec only; stays open until the Backend brief lands. DECISION: BACKEND PROXY ROUTE, NOT A WIDENED CSP ALLOWLIST. The decisive argument is structural rather than preferential — Nominatim's usage policy requires an identifying User-Agent, and useCities.ts:47 sets one on a browser fetch() where 'User-Agent' is a FORBIDDEN HEADER NAME that browsers silently drop. A direct browser call therefore can never be policy-compliant, whatever the CSP says. Meanwhile a fully compliant client already exists server-side (geocoding.service.ts: correct UA at :16, 1.1s inter-request delay at :17, ADL-10 no-requery, offline-safe) — the frontend hook is a non-compliant duplicate of a client we already own, so the proxy is consolidation, not new capability. Rate limiting is also only enforceable at a server-side chokepoint: Nominatim's 1 req/s is a per-application limit and N uncoordinated browsers is N times the rate. Bonus: proxying removes the CSP dependency entirely, so this fix cannot regress via the QUAL-18 environment-parity gap. Operational cost accepted and stated in ADL-46 section 5.1 (backend egress, caching and rate-limit responsibility, a small authenticated abuse surface). CONVERGENCE WITH BUG-63: on PO direction the same proxy route becomes the validation authority for city creation — POST /api/cities becomes resolve-then-create, building the row from the geocoder's canonical response and re-running find-or-create against THAT name, which converges 'Denverr', 'denver co' and diacritic variants that COLLATE NOCASE alone cannot. This is ADL-46 stage S2. SEQUENCING SETTLED 2026-07-28 (PO): the whole ADL-46 scope ships as ONE RELEASE rather than four dispatches, so this lands together with the BUG-63 fix rather than after it — which also closes the window where city creation would briefly have been open with only case-fold normalisation behind it.

OP-27 REVIEW 2026-07-29 CORRECTED THE RATE-LIMIT REASONING (finding F4) — the proxy DECISION stands and the reviewer did not dispute it (the forbidden-User-Agent argument carries it alone), but ADL-46's supporting evidence was wrong in a way that mattered: it claimed a reusable 1.1s limiter exists and therefore recommended NOT building one. There is no limiter object. REQUEST_DELAY_MS is a sleep() inside processQueue's for-loop, private to that function; resolveCity is exported and called fire-and-forget from POST /api/cities (cities.ts:167) with NO rate limiting at all; and each resolveCity makes TWO Nominatim requests, the isOnline() HEAD probe plus the search GET, so even processQueue already runs at roughly 2 requests per 1.1s — above the 1 req/s policy the ADL-10 comment claims compliance with. After this release there are THREE uncoordinated call sites (the 15-min queue, resolve-then-create on every POST /api/cities, and the new interactive proxy behind AddPlaceFlow's type-ahead) sharing one User-Agent and one egress IP — so a policy violation now blocks THE APPLICATION rather than an anonymous browser. Consolidating egress without building the chokepoint strictly INCREASES rate-limit exposure. ADL-46 section 5.1.1 now requires the Backend brief to build a single serialized queue through which all Nominatim egress passes, to drop or count the isOnline() probe, and to keep interactive lookups from being starved by the batch queue — or to state explicitly that it is not being built and record the accepted risk. Related: ADL-46 D10 adds a give-up rule so unresolvable names stop consuming that budget forever.

PREMISE CORRECTED, TWO PROBES: the pending/resolve machinery is NOT browser-driven — useGeocodeRetryQueue.ts's only network call is apiGet('/api/cities/:id') and its own comment says polling is read-only per BUG-29, while processQueue (geocoding.service.ts:148-192) runs from server.ts:47 every 15 minutes. The only browser-driven geocoding in the app is lookupCityCountry, i.e. this bug's path and nothing else, so Phase 2 replaces one function rather than a subsystem. ENV-01 STILL BINDS: Nominatim was re-probed from the worktree (curl exit 7) with api.github.com returning 200 from the same shell as a control — verify the proxy against a mocked upstream locally and confirm the real lookup on staging. RELATED: ADL-43 section 6.2 makes ODbL attribution a real obligation for OSM-derived data and this design increases reliance on it; a README attribution notice is flagged as its own small item, on a SINGLE probe (README.md grep only), to verify before acting.

items.title: Staging Railway environment ALLOWED_ORIGINS missing https:// scheme — CORS blocks all asset requests, white screen
items.notes: Found 2026-07-21, immediately after OP-22 closed. PO reported staging white screen + empty Turso DB. Diagnosed via read-only diagnostics (turso-query.mjs + Railway deploymentLogs GraphQL query, both per the ADL-33 runbook): Turso staging DB is fine (own separate instance, fully migrated 12/12, 250 countries seeded) — 0 users because nobody's ever gotten past sign-in. Root cause confirmed directly from server logs: `[ERROR] GET /assets/index-BGMSZVwk.css 500 CORS: origin 'https://travel-tracker-staging.up.railway.app' not allowed` (server.ts:122). Vite tags module scripts/stylesheets `crossorigin`, so the browser sends an Origin header on every asset request; CORS middleware does an exact string match against ALLOWED_ORIGINS, and the global error handler turns a rejection into a JSON 500 — browser sees wrong-MIME-type CSS + 500'd JS, i.e. white screen. EXACT ROOT CAUSE (confirmed by PO checking the Railway dashboard): Staging's ALLOWED_ORIGINS was set to the bare hostname `travel-tracker-staging.up.railway.app`, missing the `https://` scheme — `req.headers.origin` is always scheme-included, so the exact-match check in server.ts:119 never matched. FIXED 2026-07-21: PO added the `https://` scheme on the Railway dashboard and redeployed (deployment 12e1e764, 06:03 UTC). VERIFIED independently (not just PO's visual confirmation): new deployment's logs show zero CORS errors (vs. the prior deployment's immediate CORS rejection on every asset request); Turso staging `users` table now has 1 real row (`is_owner=0`, sign-in genuinely completed) — confirmed via turso-query.mjs, not just taking PO's word. CLOSED. Follow-on: this same verification pass surfaced BUG-60 (trust proxy / rate-limit misconfiguration, present in both prod and staging, unrelated to this fix).

items.title: Express 'trust proxy' not configured — express-rate-limit can't safely resolve client IPs behind Railway's proxy
items.notes: Found 2026-07-21 while verifying BUG-59's fix (deployment log review, both prod and staging). Railway sits its app behind a proxy that sets X-Forwarded-For; server.ts never calls `app.set('trust proxy', ...)`, so Express defaults to not trusting it. express-rate-limit (SEC-07, server.ts ~L147-153) detects this mismatch and throws `ERR_ERL_UNEXPECTED_X_FORWARDED_FOR` (see https://express-rate-limit.github.io/ERR_ERL_UNEXPECTED_X_FORWARDED_FOR/). CONFIRMED PRESENT IN BOTH ENVIRONMENTS via deploymentLogs: staging deployment 12e1e764 (06:05 UTC) and prod deployment f60d623b (05:45 UTC, i.e. already present in prod BEFORE any of today's changes — this is not something today's session introduced). Severity assessment: fires once shortly after boot in both environments' logs, not repeated per-request — consistent with the app being otherwise functional (prod 'confirmed working' 2026-07-21 shakedown, staging sign-in completed successfully today), so this is NOT currently a hard block on traffic. The real concern is correctness/security of SEC-07's rate-limiting: without an explicit, correctly-scoped `trust proxy` value, IP attribution behind Railway's proxy may be inaccurate (all traffic bucketed under one apparent IP) or spoofable (a forged X-Forwarded-For header trusted when it shouldn't be) depending on how this actually resolves at runtime — needs an Architect read on the correct value (e.g. `trust proxy: 1` vs Railway's actual proxy count/CIDR) rather than a guessed one-liner, since getting this wrong in the other direction (trusting an untrusted hop) is its own security hole. Per the standing project rule that runtime/infrastructure config changes need Architect ADL before COO acts — not fixed unilaterally. Affects both environments identically; one fix branch covers both once specced. RESOLVED 2026-07-22: ADL-37 — `app.set('trust proxy', 1)` (hop-count integer, not `true`; `true` would trust the whole X-Forwarded-For chain and let a client forge/spoof req.ip to bypass the rate limit, which express-rate-limit itself rejects as ERR_ERL_PERMISSIVE_TRUST_PROXY). Implemented in server.ts + mirrored in server-test-app.ts; new regression test (trust-proxy.test.ts) asserts the compiled trust predicate accepts hop 0 and rejects hop 1, not just the literal setting value. GitHub issue #221 (closed via PR #222, squash-merged, CI 9/9 green). VERIFIED LIVE 2026-07-22: Ryan approved promoting `main` → `production` (24 commits, incl. WP-01–04 Waypoint reskin + BUG-59) via the standard ADL-35 fast-forward; both envs redeployed (prod 8ca4c7fc, staging 4ff379e4) and their boot logs read clean via `railway-query.sh logs` — no ERR_ERL_UNEXPECTED_X_FORWARDED_FOR, no CORS errors, only an unrelated npm `production` config deprecation warning. CLOSED, both environments confirmed.

items.title: GET /api/admin/countries (and regions) require owner status — non-owner accounts can't populate the country picker on trip create

Map tab renders (base tiles need no API call) but with no shading and no legend key — GET /api/map/shading and GET /api/map/shading/config both 403 for non-owners, silently swallowed by the frontend. The actual blocker: TripForm.tsx's country picker (useAdmin.ts's useCountries, GET /api/admin/countries) renders empty, because that route is registered directly on adminRouter, which gates its ENTIRE router with requireOwner (admin.ts:27) — countries have no read/write split. Per GE-04/GE-05, every country ships as a global, pre-seeded default available to all users out of the box (same tier as AD-09's categories/activities, not owner-configured data) — so requireOwner on the GET path is wrong; only the admin-panel WRITE operations (PATCH country region-tier config, POST/PATCH regions) should stay owner-gated. Related but distinct from BRD-AD07/BRD-AD08 (ADL-28, per-user map shading + companions, already tracked separately, 'awaiting Backend implementation brief') — those are about making owner-only data per-user; this is about global data incorrectly gated as owner-only. Scope for this bug: split admin.ts's countries/regions GET routes to requireAuth (any authenticated user can read), keep PATCH/POST under requireOwner. Routed to Architect first per this project's established pattern for auth-scoping changes (ADL-27/ADL-28 precedent) rather than a unilateral Backend patch. GitHub issue #225. RESOLVED 2026-07-22: ADL-38 — the two GET routes (countries, regions) moved above admin.ts's router-level requireOwner guard so they're requireAuth-only; all writes (PATCH country, POST/PATCH regions) stay owner-gated below the guard, fail-closed by default for any future route. ADL-27's file stamped SUPERSEDED IN PART per the document lifecycle rule. New regression coverage in security.access-matrix.test.ts Part E (non-owner GET → 200, non-owner write → 403). PR #227, CI 9/9 green, squash-merged. Manually verified with a non-owner bypass user: GET countries 200 (250 rows), GET regions 200, writes 403, other admin routes still 403 (fail-closed intact). items.title: Admin panel is still fully owner-gated at the page/nav level — non-owner users can't reach the Companions tab even after AD-08 made companions per-user

Deliberately NOT fixed as part of PR #245 — correct fix means moving from page-level RequireOwner to per-tab gating inside AdminPanel.tsx (keeping categories/activities/shading-config-colours*/countries-regions owner-only, opening companions), which touches shared nav/route infra and reverses part of BUG-26's tested contract, judged too architecturally significant for a same-brief hook-URL fix. *Note: map shading config (AD-07) has the identical page-gating problem — its API routes are requireAuth-only per PR #243, but there's no dedicated shading-config UI tab yet to gate per-tab in the first place, so this bug's UI-side fix should cover both companions and shading config if/when a shading-config UI exists.
