items.title: Non-owner cannot add a place to a trip — categories/activities /active reads and POST /api/cities are all owner-gated (REPRODUCED + ROOT-CAUSED)
items.notes:
Reported 2026-07-26 by Ryan: two independent live sightings on mobile, both non-owner accounts. (1) A friend Ryan gave the app to reported being unable to create a trip with a forbidden-type error. (2) Ryan reproduced something matching that description himself on staging, also on mobile, around the same time — but could not reproduce it again when asked, and has no captured network response/status/screenshot from either occurrence. Distinct from the country-picker symptom raised in the same conversation, which turned out to be a separate, fully-diagnosed issue (production had not been promoted past commit c9c86f3, predating the BUG-61/ADL-38 countries-read fix and all of BRD-AD07/AD08 — fast-forwarded main→production this session to close that gap). COO investigation into THIS symptom found nothing: full non-owner-relevant backend test suite green (142/142, including security.access-matrix.test.ts Part E which is the exact regression test for this class of bug), direct local reproduction as a non-owner via BYPASS_AUTH succeeded (GET /api/admin/countries 200, POST /api/trips 201), staging's Turso DB confirmed correctly migrated, staging deploy logs show no errors around trips/companions/countries/admin since the AD07/AD08 deploy. Working theory (unconfirmed, not yet investigated): 'forbidden' may be an imprecise description of a 401 rather than a literal 403 — e.g. a mobile Clerk session/token-refresh edge case (backgrounded tab, token expiry) or an azp-origin-allowlist mismatch specific to mobile browser contexts (HC-02) — worth checking ALLOWED_ORIGINS / mobile origin handling next time this happens. Logged so this doesn't evaporate across a session boundary; Ryan is watching for a recurrence and will capture the actual network response next time. No brief until it's reproducible or a concrete lead surfaces.

REPRODUCED AND ROOT-CAUSED 2026-07-28 (Ryan, staging, desktop browser console captured). PRIORITY RAISED P2 -> P1, owner -> architect, BRD ref -> AD-09. THE 2026-07-26 WORKING THEORY ABOVE IS WRONG and is superseded: it is a literal 403, not a 401; it is not mobile-specific (reproduced on desktop); it has nothing to do with Clerk token refresh, azp, or ALLOWED_ORIGINS. Ryan was signed in as the non-owner test account and was adding a place to a trip. Three 403s in one action, one root cause — every route the add-place flow needs is behind an owner gate:
  (a) GET /api/admin/categories/active -> 403. Caller src/frontend/hooks/useAdmin.ts:34.
  (b) GET /api/admin/activities/active -> 403. Caller src/frontend/hooks/useAdmin.ts:88.
      Both are registered inside createAdminListRouter (src/backend/routes/admin.ts:147-154), whose sub-routers mount at admin.ts:232-233 — BELOW the router-level `adminRouter.use(requireOwner)` at admin.ts:105. The BUG-61/ADL-38 read/write split WAS applied to countries+regions (registered above the guard at admin.ts:61,78) but was never extended to categories/activities.
  (c) POST /api/cities -> 403. Caller src/frontend/hooks/useCities.ts:151 (apiPost). Gated by an explicit `requireOwner` at src/backend/routes/cities.ts:91. GET /api/cities is deliberately ungated (cities.ts:191-195 comment) — it is only creation that is closed, and adding a place does find-or-create.
Net effect: a non-owner cannot add a place to a trip at all, and cannot load the trip form's category/activity pickers. This is core product function, entirely broken for every non-owner — hence P1.

OP-32 CLASSIFICATION: GAP, not a regression and not deployment/config. Two probes support that: (1) code read shows the owner gates are original and deliberate, not recently introduced; (2) BRD-AD09's own tracker note (written 2026-07-28, independently) already recorded that creation sits behind the same router-level requireOwner and is 'more restrictive than AD-09 specifies, not less', parked as a future brief per ADL-28 Question 5. THAT PARKED GAP IS THIS BUG — AD-09's creation-scope gap and BUG-63 are one defect filed twice, and were not connected until now. Consolidate rather than briefing them separately.

TRAP FOR WHOEVER FIXES THIS — READ BEFORE BRIEFING: src/backend/routes/__tests__/security.access-matrix.test.ts asserts these exact 403s as CORRECT behaviour (line ~383 'GET /api/admin/categories/active -> 403', line ~414 the activities equivalent). The suite is green and is actively encoding the bug as the intended security contract. A code-only fix will be failed by CI for 'breaking' the access matrix. The access matrix (ADL-27 / jobs/architect/tech/OP-06-hardening-checklist.md section 2) must be amended FIRST, then the tests, then the code.

WHY ARCHITECT AND NOT BACKEND: neither route has a safe default. Opening POST /api/cities to any authenticated user permits non-owners to write GLOBAL shared rows — the gate is plausibly deliberate given BUG-33's find-or-create/dedup work and uniq_cities_name_country_ci, so the answer may be a constrained find-or-create path rather than simply dropping requireOwner. This is an access-matrix/SEC-01 change, which per ADL-27 and the CLAUDE.md infra guardrail needs an Architect pass before any Backend brief exists. RECOMMENDED SCOPE: bundle with BUG-55 — both are the same underlying question (which external and global-reference surfaces are reachable by whom), and answering them in separate passes risks two incoherent answers.

SPEC'D 2026-07-28 — ADL-46, GitHub issue #326 (Architect), branch chore/adl46-access-model. Spec only; no code changed, so this stays open until the Backend brief lands. THE 'GAP' CLASSIFICATION HOLDS but the framing sharpened: this is not a forgotten gate, it is SE-03 and AD-09 contradicting each other in the BRD with the code implementing SE-03 faithfully. SE-03 was already stale in two of its five clauses before BUG-63 (AD-07 and AD-08 moved shading and companions to per-user without updating it); after ADL-46 it retains none of them. Note also that ADL-38 had already called categories/activities 'the same data tier' as the countries/regions it opened for BUG-61 — in writing — and stopped one step short, which is why the deliverable's headline decision is a resource-tier rule that classifies future routes rather than three gate changes. BUG-61/62/63 are one root cause with three IDs. FIX PATH — ADL-46 Phase 1, NO SCHEMA CHANGE, clears this P1 completely: move GET /api/admin/{categories,activities}/active above the requireOwner guard (ADL-38's mechanism, but explicitly temporary scaffolding that Phase 3 deletes when those resources move to /api/categories + /api/activities), and drop requireOwner from POST /api/cities while changing nothing else in that handler — the find-or-create, country/region validation and .strict() schema are what make it safe. Implementation shape is specified in ADL-46 section 3.2 because the /active handlers are generated inside createAdminListRouter and cannot simply be moved. THE TEST TRAP IS CONFIRMED AND SPEC'D: security.access-matrix.test.ts asserts all three 403s as correct; ADL-46 section 8 lists every assertion current -> intended so the Backend brief carries authority to change them. FOUND EN ROUTE: a stale it.skip at that file's line ~457 ('PATCH /api/cities/1 -> 403', skipped pending BUG-22) is suppressing a live assertion — BUG-22 merged and requireOwner is present at cities.ts:211. Unskip it in the same brief; city curation staying owner-only is precisely what makes opening city creation acceptable. BLOCKING: GE-16 must be accepted into the BRD first or the cities half has no BRD home.

SEQUENCING SETTLED 2026-07-28 (PO): ships as ONE RELEASE, not four dispatches. The Architect recommended four phases and the COO backed that; the PO overrode it — fewer UAT rounds, no half-migrated intermediate state, one review. THIS MEANS BUG-63 STAYS LIVE UNTIL THE WHOLE RELEASE SHIPS, which was put to the PO explicitly and accepted. The four phases survive as internal build order S1-S4 (ADL-46 section 9.1) with two load-bearing constraints: S3 DELETES the admin-router carve-out S1 adds (leave it in and temporary scaffolding reaches production), and S4's city containment is meaningless without S2's resolve-then-create promoting rows. Retained as an EMERGENCY FALLBACK only, explicitly not the plan: S1 alone would clear this P1 with no schema change, if the PO ever needs an early unblock. GOOD SIDE EFFECT of the override: the Phase 1/2 window where city creation would have been open before its validation authority existed is now gone entirely.

OP-27 FRESH-EYES REVIEW COMPLETE 2026-07-29 (jobs/architect/tech/ADL-46-review.md, PR #328). VERDICT: SOUND WITH NAMED CORRECTIONS. The reviewer tried to break the access model — D1's tier rule, D3's per-user Option A, D4's curation/creation split, D5, D7 — and would not change any of them; every finding was coverage or execution. All ten accepted and folded into ADL-46. TWO BLOCKING, BOTH RELEVANT TO THIS BUG'S FIX: (F1) ADL-46 asserted trip_activities_map covered 'both trip and place level' — FALSE. Place-level activities live in trip_place_activities_map (schema.ts:376-387) and join via trip_places, not trips, so the pre-migration check returned a FALSE ZERO (reproduced on a scratch DB) and the COO's own live-data query inherited the same two-table set. The durable half: POST /api/trips/:t/places/:p/activities (routes/places.ts:242-280) validates the place then inserts a caller-supplied activity_id with NO validation at all — a permanent hole in the access model, now an explicit task. (F2) npm run db:generate emits a migration that CANNOT BE APPLIED ('Cannot add a NOT NULL column with default value NULL'), and ADL-46's stated reason for hand-writing was the wrong mechanism — name.unique() is a standalone index here, which drizzle drops happily. Instruction corrected to DISCARD the generated file rather than review it. GOOD NEWS ON THE HIGHEST-RISK ITEM: the reviewer hand-wrote the S3 recreation and EXECUTED it against a scratch DB built from the real migration chain — id preserved, trip_categories_map intact, foreign_key_check clean, on both libSQL transports including remote Turso. Validated SQL appended to the review doc. Also verified and needing no work: the Express sub-router fall-through, section 8's must-not-change 403 rows surviving S3, and the stale it.skip finding.

THREE FURTHER PO DIRECTION ROUNDS FOLDED IN 2026-07-29/30, adding decisions D10-D12 to ADL-46. D10 GEOCODE FAILURE CLASSIFICATION: a no-match response is TERMINAL on the first attempt (new geocode_status 'unresolvable'); only recoverable failures (unreachable, 4xx/5xx, network exception) retry, to a cap via a new geocode_attempts column. The distinction already exists in resolveCity's four failure branches and is discarded — all four return false and leave the row pending. isOnline()-false and GEOCODING_ENABLED=false must NOT increment, or one offline weekend burns every city's budget. COST: amending chk_cities_geocode_status is a SQLite table recreation, so S4 stops being a cheap ADD COLUMN and the release now carries THREE recreations, not two — cities is the fiddliest to reproduce (a partial index and a COLLATE NOCASE expression index, two of the four drizzle-kit bug classes ADL-15 patches). D11 CORRECTION PATH: the release creates a trap (containment + terminal state = a mistyped city is invisible, never retried, and uneditable), so it must ship the escape. Decision: make city_id updatable on a place, so correction happens at the PLACE level and never writes to a shared global row. Chosen over opening PATCH /api/cities to the creator because it has no uniqueness-collision case, preserves the place's items and activity tags, and cannot mutate a row another user shares (review P2 showed pending cities ARE shared). Delete-and-re-add already works today and needs no build. Deferred: orphan cleanup (right shape as a place-removal hook, but BUG-40/TR-15 is actively redesigning that flow — brief it with or after, never before) and creator PATCH. NOT built: a public DELETE /api/cities, and never ON DELETE CASCADE on trip_places.cityId. D12 WRONG MATCHES: containment gates on 'pending' so it does nothing about a city that resolves to the WRONG place, which bypasses containment and goes global as authoritative. Minimum adopted: constrain the lookup by the country_code CreateCitySchema already requires and the region_id it accepts (resolveCity currently sends a bare q string with no filter — the disambiguating data is already in the request and unused); user selection is NEVER overwritten by the lookup; surviving ambiguity creates 'pending' rather than guessing. No fourth status — separating 'answered' from 'verified' needs a verification actor and there isn't one at two users, so GE-16 now records that 'resolved' means a match was returned, NOT verified correct. ACCEPTED RESIDUAL RISK, stated as a decision: a confidently-wrong match entering the catalogue is currently unrepairable by anyone (PatchCitySchema accepts only region_id); the user's own experience is repairable via D11. Judged acceptable at two users, should not survive many. ALSO SURFACED, PRE-EXISTING, NOT FIXED: uniq_cities_name_country_ci has no region in the key, so the catalogue cannot hold Springfield IL and Springfield MO simultaneously — widening it naively re-opens BUG-33 because NULLs are distinct in a SQLite unique index. PO IS REVIEWING THE SPEC PERSONALLY BEFORE MERGE — plain-language summary written for that review at jobs/architect/tech/ADL-46-summary-for-PO.md.

PO REVIEW ROUND 2026-07-30 — DIRECTION APPROVED, THREE ITEMS PULLED IN, ADDING D13/D14. FRAMING CORRECTION FIRST, because it re-weights everything else: 'I don't want to be architecting based on the current user base.' The phrase 'acceptable at two users' had justified at least four judgements in ADL-46 and is WITHDRAWN wherever it appeared; each was re-weighed to either a real fix or an explicit follow-on WITH A TRIGGER. One deliberate exception recorded: the disposable-data constraint is a fact about today's database contents, not an assumption about eventual user count, so the downgrades it justified (F10 revert posture, F1's data-disposition half) stand. D13 CITY IDENTITY — PULLED INTO SCOPE: a city is now identified by (name COLLATE NOCASE, country_code, COALESCE(region_id, 0)), so Springfield IL and Springfield MO can coexist. THE COALESCE SENTINEL IS THE WHOLE POINT — region_id is nullable and SQLite treats NULLs as distinct in a unique index, so the naive UNIQUE(name, country, region_id) would permit unlimited duplicates for every non-region-tier country, re-opening BUG-33. 0 is safe because regions.id is AUTOINCREMENT (starts at 1, never issues 0). Two properties make it safe: the new key is STRICTLY MORE PERMISSIVE than the old one so no existing row can violate it (no backfill, no conflict handling), and region_id MUST be NULL when region_tier_enabled=0 (cities.ts:106-108) so for those countries the index degenerates to today's (name, country_code) exactly. THE RISKY HALF IS THE LOOKUP, NOT THE INDEX: cities.ts:126-130 becomes a three-step find-or-create — exact match on the region key, then WILDCARD-UPGRADE a region-less row (adopt it by setting its region) rather than inserting, then insert. Omitting the middle step re-creates BUG-33 through the front door. MIGRATION COST ABSORBED — the index change lands inside the cities recreation D10 already forces; no fourth migration. D14 MULTI-RESULT — DECIDED, ASK THE USER: zero candidates create pending, exactly one is accepted, two or more populate the region selector AddPlaceFlow ALREADY renders (UX-04 already fills it) rather than one being chosen silently. Chosen over 'best match' because D13 makes guessing worse (duplicates across regions are now legal, so a wrong pick creates a plausible second entry instead of colliding), because it is the cheapest fix for the stale-entry problem, and because name/region/coordinates then all come from one chosen candidate. 'Ambiguous' = more than one settlement-type candidate after the country constraint; deliberately NO confidence threshold. GE-12 not regressed — declining or being offline still creates a usable pending record. Auto-accept remains the documented fallback if the release must shrink. STALE-ENTRY LIFECYCLE ANSWERED IN FULL (ADL-46 section 4.4.3): most leftovers are NOT defects — a wrongly-matched Springfield IL is a real city with correct coordinates nobody has visited yet, indistinguishable from a seeded entry, so it stays. Unresolved creator-owned orphans go to the deferred place-removal hook. THE GENUINE GAP is the internally-wrong resolved row, which nothing collects and nobody can repair (PatchCitySchema accepts only region_id). Closed by an OWNER CATALOGUE-REPAIR SURFACE, tracked as a follow-on WITH A TRIGGER: before a third account exists. Specified as a SOFT delete (is_active, matching AD-06) so it can never orphan a trip place via the trip_places.cityId FK; the column is deliberately NOT added now despite the table being open, because an is_active nobody sets or reads is speculative generality and adding it later is a plain ADD COLUMN.

items.title: Standing docs-vs-code audit — recurring Docs brief to catch prose/reality drift before someone trips over it
items.notes: Raised 2026-07-26 out of QUAL-05's completion report (§9 follow-on) and confirmed systemic by QUAL-06. The QUAL-05 sweep was reactive — three errors were noticed by a human reading the docs, and the sweep then found more. Everything QUAL-06 cleared (project-plan.txt frozen since March, security-backlog.md asserting two resolved vulnerabilities as OPEN, an orphaned COO system prompt nothing had ever loaded, README with no mention of hosted deployment) had been wrong for weeks-to-months with no detection mechanism at all. Proposed shape: a periodic Docs brief that diffs durable-doc prose against tracker status and the actual source tree, and REPORTS contradictions only — no edits, no new tracked artefact, output is a list for COO to route. Deliberately not automated as a CI gate: the QUAL-05 experience was that classifying a sentence as state-vs-intent needs judgment, and its two branches (remove vs. supersession-stamp) were the one place the Docs agent reported the test being ambiguous. Two checks worth building in, both learned the hard way this session: (1) verify documents are LOADED, not merely that their paths resolve — audits/session-a-doc-integrity.md passed the COO system prompt as 'Clean' because 'system-prompt paths exist', and a dead document with a valid path passes that test perfectly; (2) check for status/verdict docs whose claims contradict a merged PR, which is the OP-06 failure class the Document lifecycle rule exists to prevent. Not scheduled — raise with PO when the backlog clearance plan's waves are through, since it competes with feature work for the same Docs capacity.

items.title: scripts/ci-wait.sh branch mode can PASS against the previous commit — races the mandatory post-merge main check
items.notes: FOLLOW-UP 2026-07-27 (PR #268). The first fix left an asymmetry: branch mode got a settle window for late-registering workflows, PR mode did not, because `gh pr checks --watch` was assumed to cover it. It does not — --watch returns once the checks it already knows about finish, and this repo's push + pull_request triggers register two sets at different moments. Observed live on PR #267 in the same session: ci-wait reported PASS on 9 checks, and the rollup showed 18 moments later. Benign in that instance (the late set is the identical job matrix on the identical commit, so only flakiness could differ) but it is the same fail-open shape the fix existed to close, and it was introduced by the fix rather than pre-existing. PR mode now re-watches while the check set is still growing. Deliberately, correctness does not rest on that loop terminating at the right moment: the authoritative rollup counts anything non-terminal as not-green, so an early exit yields a FAIL, never a false PASS — the loop only avoids spurious failures. ORIGINAL FIX: RESOLVED 2026-07-27 (PR #265). Branch mode now resolves the target commit from the branch itself (`gh api repos/<repo>/commits/<branch>`) instead of from run recency, then polls until runs exist for THAT SHA (bounded, DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT=180s) and exits non-zero if none ever register — 'no evidence' is now a failure, not a pass. A settle window re-queries after the first run appears so a late-registering second workflow (CI vs Security Checks) can't be missed. TIMEOUT is now an overall budget rather than a per-run allowance. CORRECTION to the original triage below: PR mode WAS affected too, by the same fail-open class — `gh pr view --json statusCheckRollup` returns an empty array before any check registers, giving `length` 0 non-green and therefore PASS; separately the non-green filter excluded `conclusion == null`, so checks still queued were silently ignored. Both fixed: zero checks is now a hard failure, and a still-pending check counts as not-green. Also found while fixing: `gh api` ignores `--jq` on an error response and writes the raw error JSON body to stdout with a non-zero exit, so a resolved SHA that is merely non-empty can actually be an error blob — guards now validate the 40-hex SHA shape rather than non-emptiness. Verified with 7 tests incl. a forced-unregistered-commit harness proving fail-closed in both modes, and a structural check that the old script contained zero branch-tip lookups. ORIGINAL TRIAGE: GitHub issue #263. Found live 2026-07-26 during the QUAL-06 close-out. In branch mode, scripts/ci-wait.sh:79 resolves its target by taking `gh run list --branch <b> --limit 1 --json headSha` — i.e. whatever the LATEST RUN happens to be — then waits only for runs whose headSha matches that. Called immediately after a merge, before GitHub has registered workflow runs for the new commit, the latest run is still the PREVIOUS commit's, which is already complete and green. It prints 'PASS — all runs green for main @ <old sha>' and exits 0 without ever waiting for the commit the caller cares about. Observed exactly this: returned PASS @ 89ad005 seconds after merging PR #262, while main was actually at 1b84557 with both CI and Security Checks still in_progress. Re-running ~30s later correctly waited and passed @ 1b84557. Severity is P1 because this is the enforcement mechanism for CLAUDE.md's MANDATORY post-merge verification ('a green PR does not guarantee a green main', BUG-24) — the one check standing between a squash-merge race and an unnoticed red main. It fails open: a genuinely red main would be reported green if the check is run promptly after merging, which is exactly when the procedure says to run it. Caught here only because the printed SHA was read rather than just the PASS. Fix direction: branch mode should take the expected SHA rather than inferring it — e.g. accept an optional SHA argument, or derive `git rev-parse origin/<branch>` after a fetch — and POLL UNTIL RUNS EXIST for that SHA (with a timeout) instead of treating 'no runs yet' as 'use the latest run'. Note ci-wait.sh:89 already has a 'No runs found for the latest commit' branch, so the not-yet-registered case is partly anticipated; the defect is that the SHA itself is inferred from run history rather than from the branch tip. PR-mode (`ci-wait.sh pr <n>`) is not affected — it resolves runs from the PR, not from run recency.

items.title: A review_pending trip has no delete affordance — TR-14 is unreachable in that state
items.notes: Found 2026-07-28 by the B7 agent (issue #316, PR #319) while implementing BUG-50, and flagged rather than fixed because the brief's file-scope anchors named only TripDetail.tsx and MobileTripDetailView.tsx. Correct call — expanding into a third file unilaterally is what OP-28 exists to discourage — but the gap is real and TR-14 is not fully satisfied while it stands. A trip in review_pending renders src/frontend/components/PostTripReview/ReviewPanel.tsx instead of TripDetail/MobileTripDetailView, and ReviewPanel has no Delete affordance, so such a trip cannot be deleted without first moving it to another status. TR-14 says deletion is 'reachable from the trip detail view' and does not carve out a status where it is unreachable. Note this is NOT the same as TR-14's deliberate Locked-trip carve-out, which is a specified refusal with a directing message; review_pending is simply an unhandled surface. Small fix: same controller wiring B7 already built, applied to ReviewPanel. Verify at the same time whether the desktop and mobile review surfaces both need it.

items.title: ReviewPanel's forward Lock path repeats BUG-58's onClose()-after-mutation pattern
items.notes: Found 2026-07-28 by the B7 agent (issue #316, PR #319) while fixing BUG-58, and correctly left alone: BUG-58 is scoped to BACKWARD status transitions and this is the forward one, so fixing it would have been unbriefed scope. BUG-58's root cause was ReviewPanel.handleReturnToPlanning calling onClose() immediately after its status mutation — onClose is wired to navigate('/trips') one level up, so the trip's :id was dropped and selection cleared in the same click that changed status. The forward Lock path in the same component has the identical shape. Whether it produces the same visible defect is UNVERIFIED — it was not reproduced, only spotted by inspection, and locking may coincidentally be a case where returning to the list is acceptable or even desired. That product question is the first thing to settle; if deselection on Lock is unwanted, the fix is the same one-line removal B7 applied to the backward path. Do not assume symmetry with BUG-58 without checking the intended behaviour.

items.title: Locked-trip delete refusal is decided from client-held status, not re-checked at confirm time
items.notes: Found 2026-07-28 by the B7 agent (issue #316, PR #319), flagged not fixed. B7's locked-trip handling branches on the client's cached trip.status when the confirm dialog is actioned, so a trip locked by another session (or another tab) after the dialog opened would be offered a delete the client believes is permitted. NOT A SECURITY HOLE and the priority reflects that: the backend is authoritative and tripsRouter.delete('/:id') returns 403 on a locked trip regardless of what the client thinks (src/backend/routes/trips.ts:429). The user-visible consequence is a raw failure instead of TR-14's specified 'refused with a message directing the user to unlock'. Low real-world likelihood in a single-user app today, but it becomes materially more likely under the shared/multi-user trip direction (FUTURE-03, tracker BUG-42 / the shared trip model), which is why it is recorded rather than dismissed. Fix direction: treat the 403 as the source of truth and render the unlock-directing message from the failed response, rather than pre-deciding from cached status.

items.title: Clerk's telemetry endpoint is CSP-blocked in deployed environments — console noise, no functional impact
items.notes: Found 2026-07-28 by Ryan during the same staging console capture that reproduced BUG-63 and confirmed BUG-55 — an organic instance of OP-32's deployment shakedown, which is what surfaced all three. clerk.browser.js repeatedly attempts https://clerk-telemetry.com/v1/event and is blocked by helmet's connect-src allowlist (src/backend/server.ts:128-130), which carries only 'self', *.maptiler.com and CLERK_ORIGIN. Logged verbatim: "Connecting to 'https://clerk-telemetry.com/v1/event' violates the following Content Security Policy directive... The action has been blocked." NO FUNCTIONAL IMPACT — this is Clerk's own product-analytics beacon, not an auth path; sign-in, session refresh and JWKS all use CLERK_ORIGIN, which is allowlisted, and the app authenticates correctly. The cost is console noise that makes real defects harder to spot during exactly the kind of shakedown that found it: the telemetry block fired four times and pushed the genuine Nominatim and 403 entries down the log. RECOMMENDED FIX — disable Clerk telemetry client-side rather than widen the CSP. Clerk's SDK accepts a telemetry opt-out on ClerkProvider; allowlisting a third-party analytics endpoint we get no value from would weaken the CSP permanently to silence a log line, which is the wrong trade under SEC-01. Small, self-contained frontend change; does not need an Architect pass, unlike BUG-55/BUG-63 which came out of the same console. Verify by re-checking the staging console after deploy — the CSP is not applied under the Vite dev server, so a local dev run cannot confirm the fix (same QUAL-18 environment-parity blind spot).

items.title: GitHub Actions pinned to v4 target Node.js 20 — deprecated, force-run on Node 24
items.notes: GitHub issue #266. Surfaced 2026-07-27 while reading main's CI logs during the BUG-64 verification (PR #265) — every job emits 'Node.js 20 is deprecated. The following actions target Node.js 20 but are being forced to run on Node.js 24: actions/checkout@34e1148..., actions/setup-node@49933ea...'. Both are SHA-pinned to v4 across 16 call sites: .github/workflows/ci.yml (8x checkout, 6x setup-node) and .github/workflows/security.yml (3x checkout, 1x setup-node). Success criteria: (1) both actions at v5 across all 16 call sites; (2) SHA pinning PRESERVED — pin the v5 commit SHA with a trailing '# v5' comment matching the existing convention, do not switch to floating tags (the pinning is a deliberate supply-chain control); (3) the deprecation warning no longer appears in any job log; (4) all CI + Security Checks green on the PR and main green after merge. items.title: Assert PRAGMA foreign_keys=1 at startup (remote Turso path verified 2026-07-28)
items.notes: Raised 2026-07-27 by ADL-41/S1 (issue #271, §11). NOT a live defect — S1 probed the installed @libsql/client and found foreign keys are ON by default (a libSQL divergence from stock SQLite), so declared ON DELETE CASCADE is genuinely enforced and TR-14's delete works as designed. This entry is the guard, not a fix: createLibSQLDb (src/backend/db/index.ts:119) issues no PRAGMA of its own, so the behaviour rests entirely on a client default that a future version bump could change silently, and every cascade in the schema depends on it. Asserting it at startup converts a silent data-integrity regression into a loud boot failure. REMOTE-TURSO HALF ANSWERED 2026-07-28 (COO): S1's premise that 'this container's firewall blocks every Turso host' was FALSE — the ADL-33/OP-21 diagnostic path is allowlisted. Probed staging via scripts/agent-diagnostics/turso-query.mjs and PRAGMA foreign_keys returns 1. Confirmed genuinely remote (libsql://...turso.io + auth token; the script has no file-URL fallback and exits if the URL is absent), so this is not a local-driver result misread as remote. Per ADL-41 §7.2's own transport analysis this reading is stronger than it looks: each statement is independently dispatched on the remote HTTP transport, so a PRAGMA read reflects the per-statement server default — the exact condition every cascade executes under. RESIDUAL: this is a pragma read on a read-only connection, not a behavioural test that an FK-violating write is rejected; the diagnostic token is read-only by design and the script refuses non-SELECT, so the conclusive version needs write credentials this environment lacks. That residual does not block the assertion. DISPATCH DECISION 2026-07-28 (PO): the assertion rides along with the B9/QUAL-03 backend brief rather than dispatching separately — same backend/test-infrastructure surface, ~15 lines plus a test. Implementation note from ADL-41 §7.2: assert (read), do NOT set — issuing PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON at connect looks like a fix and guarantees nothing on the remote transport. Success criteria: startup asserts PRAGMA foreign_keys=1 on the real application connection and fails loudly if not; remote verification recorded (done — see above).

items.title: Concurrent role dispatches collide on the single shared jobs/<role>/context/current.txt

items.title: 15 further backend test files hand-roll the same 21-table DDL that QUAL-03 just removed from test-db.ts
items.notes: Found 2026-07-28 by the B9 agent (issue #291, PR #292) while doing QUAL-03, and independently re-counted by the COO before logging. QUAL-03 made src/backend/repositories/__tests__/test-db.ts migration-derived, but 15 OTHER test files never used test-db.ts at all — they each hand-write the same 21-table DDL inline: 13 under src/backend/routes/__tests__/ (cities.get-by-id, companions, places, items.rating-sort-filter, qa-backend-fixes, items, trips.crud, owner-access, map, trip-countries, trips.delete, cities.carry-forward, security.access-matrix) and 2 under src/backend/services/__tests__/ (shading.trip-countries, shading.user-scope). COUNT CORRECTION: the agent's report said 14 (12 routes + 2 services); the actual figure is 15 (13 + 2), verified by 'grep -rl "CREATE TABLE" src/backend' minus test-db.ts and the 6 migration .sql files. Cited because the sizing matters. CONSEQUENCE — this narrows what B9 actually unblocked: REPOSITORY tests are now drift-safe, ROUTE tests are not, so the B9 report's claim that 'every other Wave 1 backend brief's tests are now trustworthy' is true only of the repository layer. Any Wave 1 backend brief whose verification rests on route tests is still verifying against a hand-maintained schema copy. The exposure is the same one QUAL-03 described and is 15x larger by file count. Note the concrete evidence this class of bug is real and not theoretical: QUAL-03's fix immediately surfaced 8 uses of an item status ('booked') that has never been valid against chk_items_status, silently green for the life of that file because the hand-written DDL carried no CHECK constraint. Success criteria: the 15 files derive their schema from the same migration-driven helper as test-db.ts; no hand-written CREATE TABLE remains in any backend test file; a deliberate migration change is detectable by route-level tests as well as repository tests; backend suite stays green with no material runtime regression. DONE 2026-07-28 (brief B4, issue #315, PR #320). All 15 files now derive their schema from test-db.ts's migration-driven helper; ~2650 lines of duplicated DDL removed. No UAT needed — test-infrastructure only, no user-visible behaviour. THIS CHORE PAID FOR ITSELF, which is worth recording against the instinct to defer test hygiene: it surfaced TWO further genuine schema-drift bugs that had been silently green for the life of their files — an invalid 'completed' trip status in trips.delete.test.ts and an invalid 'skipped' item status in cities.carry-forward.test.ts, both impossible under the real CHECK constraints. That is the same class as QUAL-03's 'booked' finding, bringing the running total to three real defects found purely by making test schemas migration-derived. The agent also PROVED drift detection now works at route level rather than asserting it: a temporary migration DROP COLUMN produced 14/14 test failures, then a clean revert. Residual: QUAL-18 is the analogous gap one layer up (the E2E environment cannot express CSP failures) and is NOT closed by this.

items.title: E2E serves the frontend from vite preview, not Express — so no CSP header is ever under test
items.notes: Found 2026-07-28 while root-causing BUG-55, on the PO's question 'should we be mirroring staging/production more closely for these tests?'. THE ANSWER IS YES AND THIS IS THE SPECIFIC GAP. Two independent probes: (1) playwright.config.ts webServer runs the frontend as 'vite preview --port 5173' with baseURL http://localhost:5173, while the backend runs separately on :3001; (2) src/backend/server.ts:233 mounts express.static(DIST_DIR) gated on NODE_ENV=production AND dist/ existing. So PRODUCTION is single-origin — Express serves the frontend document with helmet's CSP applied to it — while E2E is TWO-origin, and the document under test is served by vite preview, which sets no CSP header at all. Consequence: every Content-Security-Policy violation, including the connect-src omission that caused BUG-55, is UNOBSERVABLE in CI by construction. This is not a weak test suite; the test environment cannot express the failure. Fix: make the E2E webServer serve the built frontend through Express in production mode (single origin, helmet applied), matching prod topology. Note CI also sets GEOCODING_ENABLED=false, a second layer of the same blind spot. Success criteria: the E2E suite loads the app from the same Express process that applies helmet; a deliberately-removed connect-src origin causes an E2E failure rather than passing silently; the suite stays green and does not materially slow down.

items.title: No test asserts that external origins the frontend fetches are present in the CSP allowlist
items.notes:
Companion to QUAL-18, from the same BUG-55 root-cause pass 2026-07-28. QUAL-18 closes the class at runtime; this closes it statically and far more cheaply. The defect shape: src/frontend/hooks/useCities.ts:14 fetches https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org from the BROWSER, but that origin is absent from helmet's connectSrc at src/backend/server.ts:128-130 — nothing anywhere asserts the two lists agree. Proposed: a unit test that enumerates external origins referenced in frontend source and asserts each appears in the CSP directive that governs it (connectSrc for fetch/XHR, imgSrc for images, scriptSrc for scripts). No network, no browser, runs in milliseconds. ALSO IN SCOPE, same file, found in the same probe: useCities.ts:47 sets a 'User-Agent' header on a browser fetch(), which is a FORBIDDEN HEADER NAME — browsers silently drop it, so the app is anonymous against Nominatim's usage policy and exposed to throttling. Together these two facts argue the Nominatim call belongs behind a backend proxy route rather than a widened CSP allowlist; that is a SEC-01 decision and needs the Architect pass tracked on BUG-55, not an implementation brief. Success criteria: adding a frontend fetch to an un-allowlisted origin fails a test; the test names the offending origin and the directive it belongs in.

VALUE REVISED UPWARD 2026-07-28 after Ryan's staging console capture: the deployed environment showed TWO distinct connect-src violations in a single user action, not one. Nominatim (BUG-55) and clerk-telemetry.com (BUG-68, newly logged) were both blocked while adding a place. This test would have caught both before deploy, which makes it the highest-yield item of the QUAL-18/19/20 trio per unit of effort — reaffirming the standing recommendation to do it FIRST, ahead of QUAL-18's larger structural fix. Note the second instance also broadens the scope slightly: the offending origin came from a THIRD-PARTY BUNDLE (clerk.browser.js), not from first-party source, so an implementation that only greps our own src/frontend would have missed it. The brief should state whether third-party SDK egress is in scope and, if it is not, say so explicitly rather than leaving the gap silent.

items.title: No post-deploy smoke check — nothing verifies the deployed build behaves like main
items.notes: Third of the three environment-parity items from the BUG-55 root-cause pass 2026-07-28; implements the mechanical half of OP-32's deployment-shakedown rule. Today a green CI run says the code is correct in CI's environment, and nothing at all says the DEPLOYED artifact works — which is exactly the gap BUG-55 and the BRD-NF09 shakedown (open-dialogues D-06) both fell into. Proposed: a smoke check against the deployed URL after a staging deploy — app loads, no console errors, no CSP violations, each externally-dependent surface exercised once. IMPORTANT CONSTRAINT AND WHY THIS IS NOT BLOCKED: this devcontainer's firewall cannot reach the app's public Railway domain (D-06, still-open request), but a GitHub Action runner has no such restriction — so this belongs in CI, not in a COO-run script, and D-06 does not gate it. Deliberately scoped as a smoke check, not a full E2E run against prod: it answers 'is the deployed thing broken' cheaply and often. Success criteria: a staging deploy that serves a CSP-broken or otherwise non-functional build fails the check; a healthy deploy passes without manual steps; the failure output names what broke.

items.title: Defect taxonomy (regression / deployment / gap) + deployment shakedown before UAT
items.notes: Adopted 2026-07-28 on PO direction ('adopt now'), recorded in CLAUDE.md. Trigger: BUG-55 was briefed as a missing feature when the feature was fully built and the fault was a CSP misconfiguration — the brief would have had an agent rebuild working code and then verify it in an environment where it already worked. The PO's framing: 'this time is on me as I labelled them all UAT feedback' — the COO's assessment is that labelling was NOT the primary failure. BUG-55's tracker note had asserted 'likely the geocode/lookup path isn't wired' since 2026-07-21, an unverified single-probe absence claim that the existing negative-findings rule already covered and that one grep disproves. The rule existed; it was not applied. Two parts adopted: (1) a three-class defect taxonomy where the class determines the first action, with 'it used to work' called out as decisive evidence the COO must ASK for rather than expect the PO to volunteer; (2) a deployment shakedown before any UAT round on deployed code, plus the standing environment-parity principle — enumerate every difference between the test environment and production and treat each as an untested surface. Adopted immediately rather than logged to open-dialogues per the D-03 precedent because, unlike D-03, this has two independent incidents behind it (BRD-NF09 / D-06 and BUG-55) and a demonstrated cost. Mechanical follow-through tracked as QUAL-18/19/20.

items.title: Semgrep job pulls semgrep/semgrep:latest unpinned from Docker Hub
items.notes: Found 2026-07-27 when main went red immediately after PR #270 merged: the Security Checks / Static Analysis (Semgrep) job failed because the runner could not reach Docker Hub (registry-1.docker.io: context deadline exceeded, 3 retries) and the container never started. Not a code failure — Semgrep had passed on the identical tree 20 minutes earlier, and a re-run passed. TWO distinct concerns from one incident: (1) FLAKINESS — this is the only external runtime dependency in either workflow that is not SHA-pinned, and a registry blip turns main red for reasons unrelated to the code, which under CLAUDE.md must then be diagnosed and fixed immediately rather than left; (2) SUPPLY CHAIN — 'latest' means the analysis container can change under us with no review, while every GitHub Action in the same workflows is deliberately SHA-pinned (see DEP-03, which treats that pinning as a control worth preserving). The inconsistency is the argument. PENDING PO DECISION: raised with Ryan twice on 2026-07-27, no answer given either time — log it or leave it. Logged here rather than dropped so the question survives the session. CLOSED 2026-07-28 (PO): leave as-is, revisit only if it recurs. Two findings from the COO analysis that preceded the decision, both of which undercut this entry's original framing and must be read before anyone reopens it. (1) PINNING THE IMAGE DOES NOT PIN THE ANALYSIS. Four of the job's five --config values (p/typescript, p/react, p/nodejs, p/owasp-top-ten) are Semgrep Registry rulesets fetched over the network at scan time; only .semgrep/security.yml is local. So the job has TWO external runtime dependencies, not one, and digest-pinning the image pins the engine while leaving the rules floating. The genuinely worrying supply-chain case here is not a malicious image but rules silently disappearing and dropping scan coverage with no signal — which pinning does not touch. (2) 'ADD A RETRY' IS NOT AVAILABLE AS A CHEAP FIX. This is a job-level container: (.github/workflows/security.yml:77-78); if the image pull fails the job dies before any step runs, so there is no step for a retry action to live in. Retry-ability requires restructuring the job so Semgrep is installed within a step (e.g. pip install on a normal ubuntu runner), which also moves the dependency from Docker Hub to PyPI and allows a pinned version. IF IT RECURS, the right fix is that restructure — NOT digest-pinning, which addresses neither the observed availability failure nor rule drift and buys only cosmetic consistency with the SHA-pinned actions/*. Observed rate at closure: one incident in the project's history.

items.title: Migration 0014 preconditions are manual-only; zero-owner DB commits dangling FKs silently (review F3)
items.notes: Review finding F3, executed and reproduced against scratch DBs (not inferred). Migration 0014's §9.3.2 preconditions are documented for a human to check rather than self-enforced: on a database with zero owners the rebuild COMMITS DANGLING FKs silently, because the in-file assert is blind to missing parents; with multiple owners it assigns rows to an arbitrary one. MITIGATED FOR THIS RELEASE, which is why it did not block: the reviewer ran the live preconditions against staging AND production on 2026-08-01 and both passed (owner_count=1, zero cross-user junctions). The residual risk is the probe-to-deploy gap, and any future environment that has not been checked. Reviewer's recommendation: add an owner-count column to the assert table so the migration fails closed rather than relying on someone having run the query. Related: review F5 (LOW, doc-only) — the in-file PRAGMA foreign_keys lines are no-ops on both libSQL transports; protection comes from the driver, which wraps all pending files in one transaction and never re-validates FKs after commit. Running these files through any other runner changes semantics.

items.title: GE-16 correction-by-re-point has no UI — a user cannot fix a wrong city (UX spec MVP)
items.notes: GE-16 grants the user who created a place the right to correct it at any time by re-pointing to a different city, and states as a success criterion that a user who mistypes a city name can correct the affected place without losing its items or activity tags and without owner intervention. The BACKEND HALF SHIPPED in this release — UpdatePlaceDatesSchema accepts an optional city_id (ADL-46 D11 §4.4.2) and the re-point preserves items and activity tags. THERE IS NO FRONTEND. Verified two ways: the only place-edit surface is PlaceDateForm.tsx driven by useUpdatePlaceDates(), which is dates-only, and the UX agent independently reached the same conclusion. So BRD-GE16 is PARTIALLY DELIVERED on this criterion — same shape as the BUG-50/TR-14 precedent, and it should be read that way at UAT rather than as a pass. Scope is the UX spec's MVP (jobs/ux/tech/20260801-UX-city-entry-and-disambiguation-spec.md §12), deliberately made small: a standing 'Change city' control plus one undifferentiated 'Location not confirmed' badge with zero new hues. UX explicitly named both as NOT SAFE TO CUT — without them GE-16's correction right stays undiscoverable. UX also concluded PlaceDateForm.tsx is the WRONG surface to extend (genuinely dates-only; grafting city search onto it is scope creep) and recommends a separate, equally small modal. Everything else in that spec is deferred behind triggers — see open-dialogues D-19.

items.title: geocodeRetryQueue polls 'unresolvable' cities forever — no terminal branch
items.notes: Found by the UX agent 2026-08-01 while specifying location-status UI; verified by the COO. src/frontend/services/geocodeRetryQueue.ts documents its only exit conditions as (a) geocode_status === 'resolved', (b) 404 on poll, (c) explicit dismiss. There is no branch for 'unresolvable', which GE-16 defines as terminal, so such an entry polls GET /api/cities/:id on backoff indefinitely and never clears. NOT a GE-16 violation and not release-blocking — verified that the BACKEND queue selects WHERE geocode_status = 'pending' AND geocode_attempts < CAP, so the geocoder genuinely never re-queries an unresolvable city and that success criterion holds. The cost is wasted client-side reads plus a queue entry the user cannot clear except by dismissing. Fix is a terminal branch on 'unresolvable' alongside the existing 'resolved' one. Natural companion to UX-12, which introduces the surfacing this queue feeds.

items.title: Companion.is_active typed number but serialized boolean (third instance of the class)
items.notes: Found by the Frontend agent during the ADL-46 frontend stage while verifying response shapes rather than assuming them, and deliberately left untouched as out of scope. serializeCompanion in src/backend/routes/companions.ts returns is_active: row.isActive === 1 — a real boolean — while the Companion interface in src/frontend/types/api.ts declares is_active: number. The identical mismatch on Category and Activity was fixed in PR #341; this is the third instance of the same class and the only one remaining. Cosmetic, not a runtime defect: every consumer uses a truthy check, so 0/1 and false/true behave identically today. It is a type lie that will mislead the next person to write a strict comparison. Fold into whatever next touches that file rather than raising a standalone brief.
